bug_semantics: OpenAM's shipped iPlanetDirectoryPro SSO-session cookie is script-readable because com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly defaults to false and, through 16.0.6, has no shipped SameSite value. Any same-origin XSS can therefore read and replay the authenticated SSO token; cross-site delivery is also broader without SameSite. The OAuth/OIDC consent implementation compounded this by using that same SSO token value as the csrf form value, so script that obtains the session token also satisfies the consent check.
flaw_origin: The core insecure HttpOnly default predates reconstructable line-level history. The earliest object containing it is parentless SVN tag-snapshot commit 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e, where opensso/products/amserver/war/xml/template/sms/serverdefaults.properties:47 already says com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false. Later 5c099afa7c9361afc2f4477fec0e3018588d7840 imports the CookieUtils implementation and 94cdb6ea929e1d7232a268aacb435b86cb78a787 moves the template into the webapp; neither is a true BIC. The secondary OAuth/OIDC coupling is independently traceable to 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88, which added browser retrieval of the session cookie and comparison of csrf against ssoToken.getTokenID(), with server-side rendering added by d651c558735143384d6c183d338b535f24dd400e.
ai_marker: Unavailable: the smallest true BIC for the headline insecure cookie default is outside the available commit lineage, so there is no eligible BIC commit object from which to judge author/committer identity or AI trailers. The parentless tag snapshot, later move/import commits, the secondary OAuth commits, and the fix commit are not substitutes under the BIC-only rule.
evidence: First-party GHSA-fpmh-vx4h-xc33 states that the default configuration ships iPlanetDirectoryPro with HttpOnly=false, reuses it as an OAuth/OIDC CSRF token, affects through 16.0.6, and is patched in 16.1.1.

git grep -n -F 'com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false' 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e returns opensso/products/amserver/war/xml/template/sms/serverdefaults.properties:47. git cat-file -p 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e shows no parent and identifies it as SVN tag snapshot 'Tag for 9.5.1 RC2' at revision 389, so it cannot prove the writing commit or its immediate parent.

git log --all --reverse -S'com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false' -- . finds only parentless historical tag snapshots before 94cdb6ea929e1d7232a268aacb435b86cb78a787; git cat-file -p 94cdb6ea929e1d7232a268aacb435b86cb78a787 identifies that later commit as 'moved tempolate into webapp'. The file header itself carries an older 2009 CVS $Id, corroborating pre-import provenance. These aggregate snapshot/move objects are rejected as BICs by the audit protocol.

git show 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 shows new OAuth2ConsentPageHelper.getUserSessionId() reading CookieHelper.getCookie(config.cookieName), main-authorize.js assigning it to data.oauth2Data.csrf, and new CsrfProtection comparing request csrf with ssoToken.getTokenID(). Its parent is 3c076fc0dd1142d3c69fa39985667da2e1a8b628. git show d651c558735143384d6c183d338b535f24dd400e shows the later server-rendered data.put("csrf", token.getTokenID().toString()) path.

git grep at tag 16.0.6 finds serverdefaults.properties:52 com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false and no shipped SameSite default, plus CsrfProtection.java:47 deriving ssoTokenId, ConsentRequiredResource.java:98 rendering token.getTokenID(), and main-authorize.js:116 calling getUserSessionId(). Tag 16.0.6 peels to 4529f108e9f5d3b8f98b4afb3dd035a3c4d73a1b.

git show 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 (parent 97a34d9fee17395e8e052bfc45eb5855f436153e) removes the SSO-ID CSRF coupling, creates a 32-byte random CSRF token stored as a protected session property or HttpOnly double-submit cookie, adds org.openidentityplatform.openam.cookie.samesite=Lax, and derives the Secure flag from HTTPS. git tag --contains the fix lists 16.1.1 and 16.1.2; tag 16.1.1 peels to fe2271ec119e827b4252cec20293480322a84789.

git grep at tag 16.1.1 finds the dedicated createCsrfToken/CSRF_SESSION_PROPERTY flow and SameSite=Lax, but also still finds serverdefaults.properties:58 com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false. Thus 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 directly closes the CSRF-token reuse and missing-SameSite portions while the advisory's headline HttpOnly=false default remains present in the claimed patched release.
reasoning: A closed AI verdict requires the true BIC and BIC-only commit-object evidence. The core CWE-1188/CWE-1004 condition is already present in the earliest available parentless SVN tag snapshot and in later explicitly labeled moves/imports, so assigning any of those objects as the introducer would violate the protocol. Although the secondary 2016 CSRF coupling has a clean human-authored BIC, it is not the origin of the pre-existing script-readable SSO-cookie default named by the advisory. The direct 16.1.1 fix is identifiable and closes the CSRF coupling and SameSite gap, but it deliberately retains HttpOnly=false, making it additionally unsafe to redefine the vulnerability solely as the 2016 coupling. The missing pre-snapshot writing commit is a genuine public-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than NOT_AI or EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: The commit object that originally wrote com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false, its immediate parent, and therefore its BIC-only AI metadata are absent before the parentless 2010 SVN tag snapshot. A complete closure would require the pre-revision-389 ForgeRock/OpenSSO SVN/CVS history containing the original serverdefaults.properties change; the validated Git clone cannot supply it.
